root_cause.text: The rtmutex proxy-lock path could call remove_waiter() on an rt_mutex_waiter that was never enqueued—especially after deadlock detection in task_blocks_on_rt_mutex() leaves waiter->task unset—causing remove_waiter() to dereference a NULL waiter task.
root_cause.evidence: The commit states “task_blocks_on_rt_mutex() does not arm the waiter upon deadlock detection, leaving waiter->task nil,” and the patch adds `if (!waiter_task) /* never enqueued */ return;` in remove_waiter(), while also changing `rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock()` from `if (unlikely(ret))` to `if (unlikely(ret < 0))` so remove_waiter() is not called after a successful lock acquisition.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a null waiter_task guard in remove_waiter() to safely ignore waiters that were never enqueued.
intent_record.what: A new early-return check was added in remove_waiter() after lockdep_assert_held(&lock->wait_lock): if waiter_task is null, indicated by the comment 'never enqueued', the function now returns before entering the scoped_guard on waiter_task->pi_lock.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the function from attempting to lock or dereference waiter_task when no waiter task was ever associated with the waiter, avoiding invalid access and skipping dequeue/PI state cleanup for a waiter that was never actually enqueued.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix rt_mutex proxy-lock handling by removing the waiter only on negative error returns instead of on all nonzero results.
intent_record.what: The conditional after calling __rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock() was changed from checking any nonzero return value with `if (unlikely(ret))` to checking only negative return values with `if (unlikely(ret < 0))` before calling `remove_waiter(lock, waiter)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, `remove_waiter()` is now executed only when __rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock() returns an error code less than zero, instead of on all nonzero returns. This preserves the waiter state for positive return values that represent non-error conditions, preventing incorrect waiter removal and allowing valid proxy-lock outcomes to proceed correctly.

grouping_result.intent: Add a null waiter_task guard in remove_waiter() to safely ignore waiters that were never enqueued.
Fix rt_mutex proxy-lock handling by removing the waiter only on negative error returns instead of on all nonzero results.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by guarding remove_waiter() against a NULL waiter_task, preventing dereference of waiters that were never enqueued after deadlock detection.

The change directly targets the proxy-lock error path that could call remove_waiter() when the waiter was never properly enqueued. Restricting removal to negative error returns avoids removing an uninitialized/non-enqueued waiter after deadlock detection, matching the described root cause.

candidates.rationale: This condition treats all nonzero returns as failures requiring cleanup. In the proxy-lock path, positive/nonnegative returns can occur after deadlock detection without the waiter ever being enqueued, leading to remove_waiter() being called on an unqueued waiter.
This directly triggers the vulnerability by removing a waiter that may never have been enqueued. When deadlock detection leaves waiter->task unset, remove_waiter() dereferences that NULL task.
remove_waiter() dereferences waiter_task via waiter_task->pi_lock without first checking whether waiter->task is NULL. If called on a waiter never enqueued, this causes the NULL dereference.
This also dereferences waiter_task unconditionally inside remove_waiter(). It is part of the unsafe assumption that the waiter was enqueued and has a valid associated task.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the direct trigger of the vulnerability. In the proxy-lock path it can be reached for a nonzero return even when the waiter was never enqueued, such as after deadlock detection leaves waiter->task unset. Calling remove_waiter() in that state leads to dereferencing a NULL waiter task.

This condition is the control-flow bug that misclassifies all nonzero returns as requiring waiter removal. Positive/nonnegative returns can occur without the waiter ever being enqueued, so this check wrongly allows the unsafe remove_waiter() call.

Author: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@kernel.org>

    locking/rtmutex: Split API from implementation

    Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet contains the relevant proxy-lock start path and cleanup logic, so it is sufficient. The vulnerable construct is present in `rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock()`: after `ret = __rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock(lock, waiter, task);` it does `if (unlikely(ret)) remove_waiter(lock, waiter);`. This unconditionally calls `remove_waiter()` for any non-zero return, including negative error returns from deadlock detection. In `__rt_mutex_start_proxy_lock()`, the waiter is only enqueued via `ret = task_blocks_on_rt_mutex(lock, waiter, task, RT_MUTEX_FULL_CHAINWALK);`. Per the root cause, deadlock detection can return an error without the waiter being fully enqueued / with `waiter->task` left unset, yet this wrapper still calls `remove_waiter(lock, waiter)`. There is no guard here checking that the waiter was actually enqueued (for example by checking waiter state/task) before removing it. Therefore the buggy construct is present, and the fix is not yet in this function.
